chain.label: FAA surveillance of Aviation Charter insufficient to detect operational discrepancies
chain.trigger: although the FAA's surveillance of Aviation Charter was in accordance with its standard guidelines, it was not sufficient to detect the discrepancies that existed at Aviation Charter

chain.label: Company CRM/SOP training deficiencies; both pilots of below-average proficiency
chain.trigger: Aviation Charter was not training its pilots on CRM in accordance with its FAA-approved CRM training module... both pilots had previously demonstrated potentially serious performance deficiencies

caused_by.evidence: the POI did not detect the discrepancies that existed at Aviation Charter during his manual/procedures or training inspections

chain.label: IMC with low ragged ceilings at EVM requiring a nonprecision VOR approach
chain.trigger: the cloud bases at and near EVM were somewhere between 1,800 and 2,100 feet... clouds might have prevented the flight crew from seeing the airport

chain.label: Approach flown near MDA at about 1,800 ft, leaving little recovery margin
chain.trigger: an additional safety margin against stall and loss of control events at low altitudes where recovery is difficult, as was the case in this accident

chain.label: Late intercept vector issued close to the course at high speed
chain.trigger: The airplane's speed and close proximity to the VOR final approach course when the controller issued the 300° interception heading precluded the flight crew from completing their left turn in time to initially intercept the final approach course

chain.label: Crew not applying CRM; neither pilot monitoring instruments
chain.trigger: The evidence clearly indicates that neither flight crewmember was monitoring the airspeed indicator or CDI during the approach

caused_by.evidence: CRM was not being taught during ground school in accordance with the training manual curriculum

chain.label: Overshot the final approach course and never re-established on it
chain.trigger: the flight crew overshot the approach course almost immediately after being issued the turn... the flight crew never effectively maneuvered the airplane to remain near the approach course

caused_by.evidence: the airplane did not intercept the VOR approach course. Instead, it overshot the intended course
neither flight crewmember was monitoring the airspeed indicator or CDI during the approach

chain.label: Airplane not configured for the approach; descent begun high and fast
chain.trigger: it appears that the flight crew did not properly configure the airplane at the start of the approach (extending the landing gear or reducing power before descending from 3,500 feet)

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew was not adhering to Aviation Charter's approach procedures and was not effectively applying CRM techniques
Because the airplane was fast at this point in the approach, the flight crew had to lose a significant amount of airspeed and altitude in a short amount of time

chain.label: Failure to monitor airspeed; decay to about 76 KCAS unrecognized
chain.trigger: the flight crew failed to monitor the airplane's airspeed and allowed it to decrease to a dangerously low level... and to remain below the recommended approach airspeed for about 50 seconds. Further, the flight crew failed to recognize that a stall was imminent

caused_by.evidence: at least one of the flight crewmembers should have been monitoring the instruments
the fact that the flight crew did not properly configure the airplane at the start of the approach would have made the later stages of the approach more difficult

chain.label: Continued the unstabilized approach instead of executing the required go-around
chain.trigger: the inadequate airspeed or the full CDI needle deflection should have prompted the flight crew to execute a go-around; however, they failed to do so

caused_by.evidence: the airspeed had fallen to about 110 knots and was still decreasing, ultimately reaching a low of about 76 knots
the airplane's position relative to the VOR course would result in the CDI needle likely at full deflection approximately 2.6 miles from the VOR station

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall on final approach
chain.trigger: the airplane was at approximately 1,800 feet and slowing through about 76 KCAS, which is the approximate stall speed for the configuration in which the airplane was found

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew's failure to maintain adequate airspeed, which led to an aerodynamic stall
If the airplane does not meet these acceptable margins, the flight crew is expected to execute a go-around

chain.label: Loss of control; crew did not recover from the stall
chain.trigger: allowed the airplane to enter a stall from which they did not recover

caused_by.evidence: an aerodynamic stall from which they did not recover
stall and loss of control events at low altitudes where recovery is difficult

chain.label: Impact with terrain 1.8 miles southeast of runway 27, followed by fire
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted the ground about 1.8 miles southeast of the approach end of runway 27... A fuel-fed fire erupted after the airplane impacted the ground

caused_by.evidence: the airplane descended through the trees wings level and upright on about a 26° downward flightpath angle

chain.label: Two pilots and six passengers killed
chain.trigger: the cause of death for the pilot, copilot, and all of the passengers was multiple traumatic injuries sustained during impact

caused_by.evidence: The two pilots and six passengers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire
